core.title: Scope each train to one coherent journey
core.given: A plan contains a train and its wagons, being authored, edited, or reviewed (including an unchanged existing train or a wagon change that may alter the train's journey).
core.when: The planner sets or checks the train's outcome and which wagons it contains.
core.then: The train must tell ONE coherent journey: if its outcome cannot be stated in one sentence without 'and', split it.
prefer: Size: 3-7 wagons is the recommended sweet spot; 2 is the allowed minimum.
At 8-12 wagons, review whether the train holds multiple journeys (split if it does); at 13+, decompose.

Treat these as decomposition signals to investigate (do they mean multiple journeys?): outcome with multiple 'AND's; both setup AND teardown of a lifecycle; mix of exploratory (gesture) and core-mechanic flows; multiple independent feedback loops; participants from 3+ themes.
avoid: Trains of 13+ wagons (antipattern), e.g. a 16-wagon 'complete lifecycle' train spanning multiple journeys.
core.why: A train demonstrates one user journey end to end; bundling journeys hides independent outcomes and makes the train too large to review and accept as one story.
evidence: Reviewer states the train outcome in one sentence without 'and'.
Wagon count: 3-7 recommended, 2 minimum, 8-12 flagged for review (multiple journeys?), 13+ decompose, 1 below minimum.
Reviewer checks the train for decomposition signals; each present signal indicates the train may be multiple journeys.
verification: Scope of the check: it applies to train specs among the plan artifacts (recognized by plan-artifact kind/location per the profile); an edit confined to a single wagon's internals that changes neither train membership, outcome, flow kinds, feedback loops nor participant themes is out of scope, as are code changes that do not touch or review train specs.
Wagon count is mechanically countable and the size bands are part of the obligation: <2 below minimum, 2 minimum allowed, 3-7 recommended, 8-12 flagged for review (multiple journeys?), 13+ decompose.

The one-sentence outcome test (can the train's outcome be stated in one sentence without 'and'?) is judgment-based: a check may flag the conjunctions, but whether the train is one journey is judged, not mechanically decidable.
Decomposition signals are investigative, not auto-violations: each present signal only indicates the train may hold multiple journeys; deciding that it does (and splitting) is a reviewed judgment.

values: wagon flow kind or feedback loop changed

fires: Planner authors a new train listing its wagons and outcome.
Planner adds wagons to an existing train, pushing it to 8 or more.
Planner or reviewer reviews an existing, unchanged train for scope.
A train's outcome sentence needs 'and' to describe what it delivers.
A train has only one wagon.
A wagon edit introduces an exploratory (gesture) flow into a core-mechanic train, adds an independent feedback loop, or adds participants from another theme.
doesNotFire: Editing a single wagon's internals (e.g. wording of WMBTs or acceptances) in a way that changes neither train membership, outcome, flow kind, feedback loops, nor participant themes.
Code changes in implementation layers that do not touch or review train specs.

neutralityNotes: The core speaks the ATDD plan vocabulary (train, wagon, journey, WMBT, flow kinds such as exploratory/gesture vs core-mechanic, feedback loops, participant themes). This is method-level vocabulary assumed shared by every stack realization, not stack machinery; the only stack-dependent input is recognizing train spec files, taken from the profile via roles.plan_artifact.kinds (kind/location in the plan). The numeric size bands (2 / 3-7 / 8-12 / 13+) are the obligation itself and stay in the core rather than becoming profile data. The named-check/term ids (one_journey_test, decomposition_signal) and the project-specific calibration train ids (train:decision:standard, train:match:solo-match-complete) have no stack-neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; the core's verification names those checks generically. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so none is asserted in the core's verification.
